correctness.rationale: Complete constructive proof for every finite horizon: singleton approval reduction, sorted minority counts, both exact cases of t, floor inequalities after unanimous rounds, monotone refinement from nonempty ballots, Pareto-efficient completion by finite DP, and explicit |S|=1,2,3 quota checks. The computations are corroboration only, not proof of infinite scope.

originality.rationale: The exact original strong-core definition is the substantive common object. Phillips et al. establish its general nonexistence and only one-way implications to weaker axioms, not a universal three-voter binary positive theorem. The arbitrary-horizon balancing lemma, two-quota thresholds, and Pareto completion are not supplied by the inspected sources. Published mathematical-record results compared are about distinct static voting or allocation questions. No perfect novelty guarantee is asserted; unindexed priority remains a documented risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed earlier three-voter binary core theorem or an equivalently strong public-decision theorem may exist.
Secondary related articles were compared by abstracts, not all full texts.

value.rationale: sCore is a substantive coalition-resistance axiom known unsatisfiable without restrictions. The natural 3-voter/2-alternative boundary admits an exact all-horizon positive existence theorem and polynomial construction; it resolves simultaneous single-voter, pair-quota, and full-grand-coalition constraints, rather than a textbook exercise or a weak-JR renaming. No broad theorem beyond the stated domain is suggested.
